data.narrative:
Astera Labs is a public-stage semiconductor company that has raised $713M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of four same-sector, same-stage peers: Cerebras ($39.2B), Credo Semiconductor ($35.8B), Ouster ($2.3B), and Aeva Technologies ($1.1B), spanning a range of $1.1B to $39.2B.

The peer-median method is the primary applicable triangulation approach, given data constraints. The median valuation across the four public semiconductor peers is $19.0B. A revenue-based approach (P/S anchoring) cannot be applied because Astera Labs' revenue figures are not on file; this is typical for private companies and creates a material information gap. The peer median therefore anchors the analysis absent direct financial metrics.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $16.2B (low) to $21.9B (high), with a median of $19.0B. This range reflects the dispersion inherent in the peer set—the presence of outliers at both ends (Cerebras and Aeva) introduces meaningful uncertainty. The analysis is constrained by reliance on a single applicable method and the absence of revenue or profitability data. Valuation credibility would improve substantially with disclosure of Astera Labs' top-line metrics and gross margins relative to the peer universe.
